message:
Jim: extremely well said, particularly your third paragraph. And Jim's point, Sarah, demonstrates that the profits Elsevier harvests from the labor of academics, in their flow to parent corporation Reed Elsevier, implicate academics who publish with Elsevier in Reed Elsevier's facilitation of the international arms trade -- which, as Jim points out in his second paragraph, seems rather less defensible than the corporate talking points  you offer make it out to be. Jim, can I ask you to cross-post your comment to [the Kairosnews discussion](http://kairosnews.org/node/4419), as well?

And Charlie, I agree, but I'll also note that it's unfortunately not uncommon. In my dissertation work, I've noticed in our disciplinary literature an eagerness to rhetorically construct economic inequality as an essentially unchangeable phenomenon, in order to get off the hook in terms of actually having to go out and make some change. Easier to bemoan the impossibility of change than to actually go out and work for possible change.
